Thanks for the MAP draft — we reviewed the milestones and want to confirm the performance gating for our production rollout. Two quick asks before we finalize the timeline:

1) Can you share a short summary of the latency p50/p95 and sustained throughput you expect for our workload (avg 512 tokens context, bursty 20 reqs/s)?
2) If we hit the P50/P95 targets, what tuning steps and lead times are typical if we need to push the latency down another 20%?

We are on a tight close window: our procurement lead needs a recommended final SLA/price by 3/25 to align with the Q2 board ask.

Appreciate a short checkpoint this week.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance targets and close window

Rachel — thanks, and good context on the timeline. Attaching a short summary and raw export from our benchmark run. High level answers below; attachments: latency_results_q1_2027.csv, MAP_v2_close_timeline.xlsx.

Summary (512-token context, mixed prompt/content style close to your dev load):
- Baseline (open-model v3 quantized q4_0): p50 = 42 ms, p95 = 128 ms, sustained throughput = ~18 req/s per GPU; peak batching can push short bursts to ~30 req/s for 64-token outputs.
- End-to-end application (network + runtime, from our hosted eu/us region tests): p50 = 65 ms, p95 = 185 ms. Your on-prem network might add ~10-25 ms depending on routing.

Tuning path if you need ~20% lower latency: (estimated 2–3 weeks for validation + canary)
- Short term (3–5 days): enable optimized attention kernels + continuous batching limits -> expect 8–12% improvement. (Owner: Rafael)
- Mid term (1–2 weeks): quantization profile shift (from q4_0 -> q4_alt) and KV cache priming for common prefixes -> additional 6–10%. (Owner: Priyom)
- Longer term (~2–3 weeks): model variant swap to a lower-latency topology (smaller param variant or distillation) + updated kernel tuning -> up to 20% but requires model validation. (Owner: Monica / Eng)

Immediate action items from our side: 
- AI-1: Share raw CSV + annotated metrics (attached) — Monica (today)
- AI-2: Run a 24-hour sustained throughput test with 512-token tail latencies and include network emulation — Priyom (target 2027-03-18)
- AI-3: Draft canary rollback windows and kernel toggles for fast rollback — Rafael (target 2027-03-19)

Commercial note: Marcus will propose a recommended SLA/discount stanza tied to the MAP milestones by 3/23 — that should feed your procurement ask on 3/25.

Let us know if 3/18 for the 24-hour throughput report works; we can run it in your region if you prefer.

Best,
Monica Patel
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[monica_patel@redwood.com]

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 10:05 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary (...)

Adding technical detail from the 48h run:
- Observed median kernel time for attention ops was 28ms; swapping to the fused attention kernel reduced that to ~20ms for 512-token seqs (measured on A100-80GB equiv).
- Batch-shaping: we saw best p95 improvements when limiting micro-batches to 4 concurrent requests per batch for your workload shape; higher concurrency increases p95 tail due to longer queuing.

Proposed canary steps (short):
1) Canary-1 (non-prod): enable fused attention + small-batch shaping; run 6-hour smoke -> rollback flag ready (Rafael)
2) Canary-2 (prod-lite): 2-hour rollout to 5% of traffic with prefetched KV cache; monitor p95 and error rate -> rollback if p95 regression > 10% (Rafael + Priyom)

Estimated lead times: Canary-1 = same day (6–8 hours); Canary-2 = 1–2 days to schedule with infra. I've added detailed notes to canary_plan_notes.md.

[Attachment: canary_plan_notes.md (text/markdown, 6KB)]
